findings.where: Screen 9 (Where the power goes), the demonstration
findings.what: After Hold true power goes off, the scripted sweep only takes φ from 72.5° to 90°, so Dan never sees the power wave at 0° (never dipping below the line) or its dip growing from nothing, which the after-text describes; a sweep from 0° to 90° would show the cause without him having to drag.

findings.where: Screens 1, 3, 9 and 10 in light mode: the V and I arrows and the V and I waves
findings.what: In light mode the voltage stroke (ink #1F2937) and the current stroke (accent2 #17324D) both look dark navy, so at 0° on screen 1 the two arrows read as one, and on screen 9 the key's V and I swatches cannot be told apart; give the current a clearly different colour or label the two waves on the strip.

findings.where: Screens 7 to 9, the plot of current against power factor
findings.what: The current axis has no values, so the dot and its dashed guide cannot be read off the plot; ticks at 43.5, 72.5 and 145 A, or a label on the dot, would let the plot show the 43.5 to 72.5 to 145 A rise on its own.

findings.where: Screen 7 (Hold the true power), the angle label on the held triangle
findings.what: On the small held triangle the "53.1°" label sits outside it, just right of the dashed upright side and directly above "13.3 kVAr", so it reads as belonging to the upright side and not to the corner on the left.

findings.where: Screen 3 text, and the explain paragraph on the power triangle
findings.what: The upright side, "1992 VAr ... the energy that goes back and forth", calls a rate an energy; "the rate at which energy goes back and forth" would be accurate for an HNC reader.

The interactive says the floor shadow is in step and then calls V × floor shadow the true power, but why the wall shadow delivers nothing on average is only shown six screens later on screen 9; one sentence on screen 3 (it carries energy in and back each cycle, so on average it delivers none, and screen 9 shows it) would close the gap inside the interactive.
The after-paragraph giving 10 cos 60° = 5 A and 8.66 A is shown from the first frame while the current arrow still lies along V at 0°, so the numbers arrive before the swing they describe.

findings.where: Screens 11 to 13, the ask line after Why?
findings.what: Opening Why? at the tool stage skips straight to the answers, and the ask line then reads "The cosine rule it is. Now pick the answer." as if Dan had picked that tool himself.
